props.title: Happy ==Code== Library
props.subtitle: Code that makes you smile — and teaches while it does.
props.foot: A browsable library of small, joyful code examples

slides.notes: Open warm. This is a library of tiny code examples designed to spark delight — the point of this deck is that delight is a teaching strategy, not decoration.

props.title: Example code is too often ==dry==, intimidating, or buried.
props.body: Beginners bounce off walls of terse snippets. And even experienced developers learn better from examples that spark a little delight.

slides.notes: Land the pain: nobody curls up with API reference code. When examples feel like homework, learners stop — and that's true at every skill level.

items.title: Small enough to finish
items.body: Every example reads in about a minute — one idea, no scaffolding to wade through.

items.title: Playful enough to remember
items.body: A little humor and personality make the pattern stick long after the tab is closed.

items.title: Annotated to teach
items.body: Each snippet explains the lesson alongside the code, so the takeaway travels with you.

slides.notes: Three commitments: short, fun, annotated. Curated — every example earns its place. That curation is what separates a library from a snippet dump.

props.title: From browsing to ==borrowing== in four steps.

items.title: Browse by topic or mood
items.body: Pick a subject — or pick a feeling. "Feeling playful" is a valid search query.

items.title: Open an example
items.body: One small, runnable snippet with its annotations — nothing else on the page.

items.title: Read the happy path
items.body: See the one clean way the idea works, with the lesson written next to it.

items.title: Take the pattern with you
items.body: Copy it, remix it, ship it. The pattern is yours now.

slides.notes: Walk the loop quickly — the mood-browsing detail is the memorable one. The happy path framing is deliberate: we show the one clean way, not every edge case.
The core argument: examples people enjoy are examples people finish, share, and build on. Joy isn't garnish — it's the mechanism that gets the lesson to stick.

tiles.title: Runnable
tiles.body: Copy, paste, run. Every example works as shown.

tiles.title: Annotated
tiles.body: The lesson is written right beside the code.

tiles.title: Mood-browsable
tiles.body: Find examples by topic — or by how you want to feel.

tiles.title: Tiny by design
tiles.body: One-minute reads. One idea per example.

tiles.title: Made to share
tiles.body: Link an example, send it to a friend, fork it freely.

slides.notes: Hit the highlights: runnable, annotated, browsable by mood, tiny, shareable. The constraint is the feature — smallness is what keeps people reading.

props.caption: open source — a growing library, built in the open and better with every contribution

slides.notes: The library is live and growing, fully open source. Invite the audience: the best way to get the example you wish existed is to add it.

props.title: Go write something that ==smiles== back.
props.subtitle: Browse the library, borrow a pattern, leave one behind.

slides.notes: Close with the call to action: visit the repo, find one example that makes you smile, and pass it on. Contributions welcome.
